**Title:** Evidence at What Cost? Decoupling and Scaling in LLM-Based Document Relation Extraction

**Abstract:** LLM-based Document-level Relation Extraction (DocRE) now matches or exceeds encoder baselines in extraction accuracy, yet these methods output bare relation triplets without identifying supporting sentences. Encoder-based evidence methods (SAIS, DREEAM) provide supporting sentences but trail LLM approaches in accuracy, creating a gap between extraction performance and output verifiability.

We formalize evidence-grounded DocRE as structured generation and compare GRPO, DPO, and RSFT across three fully evaluated scales (1.7B, 4B, 8B) with 14B validation, two model families, and two datasets. The evidence tax—extraction cost of generating evidence—is scale-dependent: beneficial at 1.7B (−5.63pp dev Ign-F1) but approximately neutral at ≥4B (+0.25±0.47pp at 4B; positive = cost). Gradient-based optimization amplifies evidence-extraction competition (GRPO catastrophic, DPO gradual), while RSFT with NLI-based scoring avoids decoupling entirely through output filtering rather than gradient pressure.

RSFT consistently reduces training seed variance (complete pairwise seed separation on LLaMA, Cohen's d=2.58; non-overlapping χ² CIs at 1.7B). Our 1.7B RSFT model (51.19 Ign-F1, std 0.09pp) approaches 8B SFT performance (50.19, std 3.23pp) at 4.7× fewer parameters. Test-set evaluation preserves model ranking across all evaluated scales (Spearman ρ=1.0).
